A shower with no deposit is left out of both sums. The sampling fraction it implies is 100 / c. Interval: 95% Student-t on the linearised ratio, events as clusters (n − 1 d.o.f.), clipped at zero because c is a ratio of non-negative sums.

whisker.label: 95% χ² interval of σ divided by μ, [σ_lo/μ, σ_hi/μ] (N − 1 degrees of freedom): never negative, and skewed upward as the sampling distribution of σ is at small N. μ's own uncertainty is neglected; the delta-method standard error of σ/μ, which includes it, is se_delta. The χ² interval of σ itself is sigma_ci95, in the series' own unit.

resolution.note: σ/μ in percent per 1 GeV bin of the shower's own momentum, from the unbiased (ddof = 1) width. Calibrated energy: c · E_dep with c fitted once over the whole selection. It includes the spread of the momentum inside the bin, σ_p/⟨p⟩, which alone gives σ/μ = 58% in a bin that spans 0–1 GeV. Response ratio: the spread of E_dep / p, which divides the momentum out and does not change with c. Below N = 15 the bias factor c4(N) of σ is quoted; below N = 20 the Gaussian-shape verdict is untestable and the bin is weak.

notes: Each shower's deposit E_dep is the truth segmentation's share of the event's hit energy (a cell both showers hit is divided by the truth fraction) and p is that shower's own incident momentum. Showers A and B are separate series with one value per event each; an event in which a shower has no hit rows is not part of that shower's series.

The sampling fraction is f = E_dep / p per event and shower, in percent. A value no ratio can use is counted and dropped, never zero-filled. Every mean, SD, ratio and interval is taken over all the events of its series or bin; a display range clips the picture and nothing from the statistics.
